newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end firm amid profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end firm amid profit-taking.

text.p: Singapore shares ended firm on Wednesday despite profit-taking in several stocks, said dealers. "The market was fairly active. Some banks and properties like CityDev and Wing Tai, which looked attractive at current valuations, continued to see buying interest," a dealer said. CityDev and Wing Tai rose Singapore $0.30 and S$0.06 respectively to end at $11.90 and S$3.70.
"But the feature of the day was a reasonable amount of profit-taking," the dealer said. "This is because there has been no fundamental change in Singapore's economy and corporate outlook."
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended at its day high at 2,146.48, up 18.63 points. Market turnover was active at 162.4 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 200 to 141.
Malaysian Samanda Holdings led losers, shedding S$0.40 to S$7.30 as investors feared a correction in the Malaysian bourse.
Profit-taking led Creative and Total Access Communications lower by S$0.15 and US$0.20 respectively to S$8.30 and US$6.55.
Cycle & Carriage and Sea View Hotel topped gainers, rising S$0.70 and S$0.40 respectively to S$15.10 and S$14.00.
